All contributions are welcome: bug reports, feature suggestions, code, translations, and documentation.

## Code of Conduct

Be respectful and constructive. This is a project aimed at children — keep the tone friendly and inclusive.

---

## How to Report a Bug

1. Check the [existing issues](https://github.com/RoTteNnSS/DrawingKidsGame/issues) to avoid duplicates.
2. Open a new issue using the **Bug Report** template.
3. Include:
   - Steps to reproduce
   - Expected vs actual behavior
   - Windows version and .NET version (`dotnet --version`)
   - Screenshots if relevant

---

## How to Request a Feature

1. Open an issue using the **Feature Request** template.
2. Describe the use case and why it would benefit users (especially kids!).

---

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

- Windows 10 or later (64-bit)
- [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download)
- Visual Studio 2022/2026 with the **Desktop development with .NET** workload

### Steps

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RoTteNnSS/DrawingKidsGame.git
cd DrawingKidsGame/ColorKids
dotnet build DrawingKidsGame.csproj
```

Open `DrawingKidsGame.slnx` in Visual Studio for the full IDE experience.

---

## Branch Strategy

This project uses **GitHub Flow**:

- `master` is the **stable, protected branch** — never push to it directly.
- All work (features, fixes, docs) must go through a **Pull Request**.

### Branch naming convention

| Type | Pattern | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| New feature | `feature/<short-description>` | `feature/stamp-tool` |
| Bug fix | `fix/<short-description>` | `fix/flood-fill-crash` |
| Documentation | `docs/<short-description>` | `docs/update-readme` |
| Refactoring | `refactor/<short-description>` | `refactor/bitmap-service` |

### Workflow

```bash
# 1. Fork the repo on GitHub, then clone your fork
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/DrawingKidsGame.git
cd DrawingKidsGame/ColorKids

# 2. Create a branch from master
git checkout -b feature/my-feature

# 3. Make your changes, then commit
git add .
git commit -m "feat: describe what you did"

# 4. Push your branch
git push origin feature/my-feature

# 5. Open a Pull Request on GitHub targeting master
```

---

## Pull Request Guidelines

1. Base your PR on `master` (never on another contributor's branch).
2. Keep changes focused — one PR per concern.
3. Make sure the project **builds without warnings** (`dotnet build`).
4. Write a clear PR description explaining *what* and *why*.
5. Reference related issues with `Fixes #<number>` when applicable.
6. A PR will be reviewed and merged by the maintainer — be patient and open to feedback.

---

## Coding Standards

- Follow existing file and namespace conventions (`DrawingKidsGame.*`).
- Use **C# 13** features where the TFM (`net10.0-windows`) supports them.
- Prefer `internal` / `private` over `public` — least-exposure rule.
- No unused parameters or methods.
- Async methods must end with `Async` and accept a `CancellationToken`.
- Keep UI strings in English (the project targets English as the base language).
- Do **not** edit auto-generated files (`*.g.cs`, `// <auto-generated>`).
